national.title: "The Mosquito Bowl" and the human cost of war
national.summary: Director Peter Berg discusses his new film, the true story of All-American football stars who volunteered for the Marines and fought in the Battle of Okinawa, the last and costliest World War II battle in the Pacific.
national.body: Okinawa proved to be the last and costliest battle of World War II in the Pacific – and it's a name director Peter Berg wants us all to remember. His new movie, "The Mosquito Bowl," captures that battle. "It is a film that I hope asks us all to look at what we ask of our young men and women," he said."The Mosquito Bowl" is based on the book by Buzz Bissinger, who also wrote "Friday Night Lights," which became Berg's breakout movie. But don't let the title fool you – it's not a movie about a football game. "No, it's not; it's a movie about the cost of war, the human cost of war," said Berg. The human cost of war as told through the true story of four All-American football players who volunteered for the Marines after Pearl Harbor, and reported to boot camp at Parris Island, South Carolina, which is where we interviewed Berg. "They came down here and they joined the Marine Corps, thinking, Hey, we'll go win this thing. We'll go whup some butt and win this thing, like we win our football games," Berg said. "Then they come across an enemy, the Japanese, who are instructed by their emperor, who they believe is a god, to not surrender."They first encountered the Japanese on a tiny speck of coral called Tarawa. When footage of American dead on the beach at Tarawa reached the United States, the public saw for the first time the human cost of war. It's the first battle sequence in the movie."I wanted it to be as hard and as intense as I could possibly make it," Berg said. "I wanted it to feel terrifying, because that's how I believe it was."Berg's immersive style of filmmaking uses real flame throwers and real explosions. It's also his style of research. For "Friday Night Lights," he spent a season with a high school football team in Texas. For "Lone Survivor," he spent a month with Navy SEALs in Iraq.He wrote most of the script for "The Mosquito Bowl" on Parris Island. "Just gets into your blood," he said. "And then I carry that, I try to, onto the set. And that's why I don't worry about the marks, I don't care if your jacket looks perfect, I don't care about the lighting; I want the soul."For Berg, these recruits at Parris Island are the human cost of future wars. "It's a very, very powerful force," he said. "It's a very dangerous group of human beings. national.title: At least 12 injured, including 6 children, in shooting near Florida A&M
national.summary: Police say a fight broke out before the shooting.
national.body: At least 12 people were injured, including six children, in a shooting Saturday near a football stadium in Tallahassee on homecoming weekend for Florida A&M University, authorities said. Eleven people suffered gunshot wounds.Tallahassee police said in a statement Sunday that six of the shooting victims remained hospitalized, and five had been discharged. One of those still hospitalized was being treated for critical injuries.The department previously said at least three people sustained serious injuries in the shooting, while nine others are reported to be in stable condition.The preliminary investigation indicates that a fight broke out before the shooting, according to police. It followed a football game in a crowded area.Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence Revell told reporters that no arrests had been made."Tonight, our thoughts are with the victims and their families as they face the devastating impact of this violence," said Revell. "It is especially heartbreaking to know that children are among those injured."The university said on social media that the shooting happened near its campus and that it remained safe.

national.title: Parker Posey: "I have felt in the right place at the right time"
national.summary: In the 1990s actress Parker Posey was dubbed "The Queen of the Indies." The Emmy-nominated star of "The White Lotus," and the new film "Wild Horse Nine" talks about her Southern upbringing, and how her parents inspired her acting.
national.body: This was actress Parker Posey's first headshot as a teenager. "How cute is this?" she laughed. It's been a long time, but I still see this girl. "I'm still that girl, are you kidding?" she said.I met that girl in 1985, when we were both 16, at the North Carolina School of the Arts in Winston-Salem. "We were serious young performers," she said. It was a decade before Parker Posey became one of the breakout stars of the 1990s independent film heyday. We met at a loft which was the very first place she stayed on a trip to New York City. But she's very much a product of her Southern upbringing – and the two people she calls the stars of her family. "My dad would take my mom on dates," she said. "They would go to the grocery store, 'cause they didn't have money, and he would make up stories of the people going in and out of the grocery store to make my mom laugh. So, entertain yourself! And if you can't, work on it, you know?"And that's what Posey has been doing with particular relish throughout her career. Whether the part is big or small, there's always the sense that she's having fun with it, whether it's "Dazed and Confused," "You've Got Mail," "Josie and the Pussycats," or "Scream 3."Parker Christian Posey and her twin brother were raised in Monroe, Louisiana, and Laurel, Mississippi. Her mother Lynda was a chef, and her late father Chris owned a car dealership. Her Southern roots came in handy for season three of "The White Lotus," where Posey was Emmy-nominated for her portrayal of the pill-popping and much-quoted North Carolina matriarch Victoria Ratliff.Was any part of that character her mom? "Oh, my God, of course!" she laughed. "It was all the women in my family, and some people that – I mean, I love the drama that the South brings. I remember being in a grocery store and I just thought this woman was hilarious, and she goes, 'Do you have the ROH-maiiiiiine lettuce?' You're just like, Wow! 'ROH-maiiiiiine'!" Posey spent several of her summers working at her father's car dealership: "I was always imitating people and putting on accents. I liked speaking over the speaker. And I'd say, "Good morning. national.title: Ghost signs: Fading reminders of the past
national.summary: They're painted advertisements from long ago, for businesses that may have since died. But remnants of these "ghost signs" still remain, haunting our urban spaces – and one artist is bringing ghost signs back to life.
national.body: On the streets of Schenectady, New York, Ron Ladouceur is "ghost hunting" in broad daylight, alongside an old brick wall. "We've got a couple of letters we can make out here, right?" he said. "There's the word 'service,' that's pretty clear. The brand name was here. This was probably an auto service center of some sort."These faded advertisements, known as ghost signs, are all around us, often hiding in plain sight."It's very much a ghost," Ladouceur said. "It pops out, and all of the sudden, they start popping out from alleyways and other buildings, and you're like, Ah! You're haunted by them, and you have to go find more. It becomes an obsession."Ladouceur is an adjunct professor of marketing at the University at Albany. For him, these brick walls are windows into the past. "The golden era of ghost signs is anywhere between about 1895 and the 1930s," he said. "It really coincides with the rise of national advertising." While you can find faded signs for brands like Coca Cola, Ivory Soap, and Wrigley's gum, most ghosts promote companies, products and brands that died long ago. It's as if they have unfinished business. Some are barely decipherable – like a puzzle to be solved. "Absolutely, I mean a lot of them are almost unreadable," Ladouceur said. "Many of them have been painted in layers, because they were a good advertising spot, so people would paint over it with a new ad, new ad, new ad. And now they're fading in sequence."Occasionally, a vibrant "new" ghost sign makes the news when one is uncovered after a siding is removed, or a neighboring building is torn down. But overall, we're losing them due to demolition. Ghost sign aficionados have been cataloging these phantasms before they disappear forever. But one artist has been bringing them, ever so briefly, back to life. Craig Winslow's "Light Capsules" project utilizes projection mapping to recreate what a ghost sign might have looked like in its heyday. "It's one night we are, like, conjuring up all of this magic energy and opening this time portal and seeing what these old ghosts have to say," said Winslow. "This art does not exist without the wall itself. It doesn't exist without the painter that did that back then, and I feel kind of almost like a medium. national.title: Israeli election to test Benjamin Netanyahu's ability to hold power
national.summary: On Tuesday, Israel will hold its first parliamentary elections since the October 7, 2023 terror attacks. Essentially one man is on the ballot: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. How might Israeli policy change if the opposition succeeds?
national.body: Tens of thousands marched in Tel Aviv last night demanding Benjamin Netanyahu's government answer for the failures that led to the October 7 terror attacks. "We cannot be a dictatorship!" said one woman. "And we cannot have these criminals running our country." Tuesday will be the first parliamentary elections since the attacks. Thirty-nine parties are running, but essentially one man is on the ballot: Netanyahu. Over three decades, Netanyahu (known here as Bibi) has dominated Israeli politics.And in a market outside Tel Aviv, opinions about the prime minister are as varied as the offerings here. Asked whom he will vote for, restaurant owner Benny Abraham replied, "Likud and Bibi Netanyahu.""Bibi can handle the whole world," Abraham said. "Bibi is charismatic. He has a strong voice. The world loves him." He added affectionately, "He's the king of Israel."Many others, like Liat and her husband Sharon, could be lumped into the "Anyone but Bibi" camp. "I don't hate him, OK, I think he did the good things to Israel, but no more," said Liat. Sharon described Netanyahu as "more or less, very good politician, but not a [good manager]." The divide on Netanyhu stems from controversial changes sidelining the country's judiciary; an ongoing trial on corruption charges; and allegations he failed to heed prior warnings about October 7. While some people says they feel Netanyahu protects Israel, 80-year-old Margalit Moses told us she does not feel the prime minister protect her. Moses was kidnapped by Hamas on October 7th. Nearly a third of the residents of her kibbutz, Nir Oz, were killed or captured. October 7th moved many Israelis further to the right – but Moses. "I hope people will understand that we have to change the government so the new government will be more middle, or a little bit left," she said. "We'll change the mind in Israel about the Arabs. If we can make peace with them and live in peace with them, it's, for me, very important."Netanyahu's campaign has framed these elections as existential for Israelis. national.title: 100 years later, the mystery of Houdini's death endures
national.summary: Harry Houdini, the greatest escape artist who ever lived, died 100 years ago on Halloween – a fact that has only burnished his image as a daredevil who often cheated death. But was there a cover-up involving the circumstances of his death?
national.body: Harry Houdini, the greatest escape artist who ever lived, has been the subject of hundreds of books and movies. A pop icon, even today. He died 100 years ago this week, on Halloween – a coincidence that did nothing to diminish his mystique. But we'll get to that.Erik Weisz was born in Hungary, in 1874. When he was four, the family moved to Wisconsin. As a teenager, he performed magic tricks in sideshows and beer halls. "He was a skinny kid, and he built himself up," said New Yorker staff writer David Denby. "He became this beautiful, incredible body, and he was a handsome man."But according to Denby, he wanted a catchier name. He turned to his idol, Houdin, the great French magician of the 19th century: "So, he took the name Houdin and added an i and pronounced it as Houdini. But the name always sounded funny. It's vaguely Italian, but it's not. What is it?"Houdini historian Roger Dreyer owns one of the world's largest collections of Houdini artifacts, such as the Metamorphosis Trunk. He says Houdini's magic tricks didn't exactly bring the house down. "If he was to perform it today, he wouldn't even make it past the second round on 'America's Got Talent,'" Dreyer said. "It wasn't until his Metamorphosis Trunk that Houdini really became bookable; theaters wanted to see his act. People today, over 100 years after Houdini's death, still perform this exact same trick."After being locked in a trunk, Houdini switched places with his new wife, Bess, instantly. But once he added handcuff escapes to his show, Houdini became a sensation. Denby said, "He would be put in a cell, virtually naked, shackled. He'd come out 20 minutes later holding the handcuffs. The specialists were called out of their corners to produce the most complicated locks for him. He'd lick it every time. There's no record of his failure."Denby says there was symbolism in his escapes: "He would defeat those police forces all over the world. And so, there was definitely a kind of anti-authoritarian message that people liked."In time, the act was more than escaping shackles. It became about escaping death. "He always reinvented himself," Dreyer said. "Initially, he got out of a trunk. Then Houdini got out of a straitjacket. Then Houdini would get out of a straitjacket hanging from a crane. national.title: Poll finds Democrats still boosted by voters' economic concerns
national.summary: President Trump is a key factor driving support and opposition; turnout looms large
national.body: Call it the "avoidance" election, with many on each side more motivated by trying to prevent or stop things than by what they'll gain.Against a backdrop of continued concern about inflation and the economy, Democrats maintain their lead in a bid for a House majority. They're currently on pace for 229 seats in our CBS News House model estimate, which translates voters' congressional preferences into seats. The potential range of outcomes could reach into the 230s in our model, but Republicans do still have a very narrow path to hold the majority, too.While that Democratic lead has been durable over recent weeks, it hasn't expanded, either. In other words, there isn't a growing wave, at least not as of today. If anything, the still undecided or uncertain voters tend to profile as more Republican. Whether they decide to show up is perhaps the key question of 2026.Either way, voters describe a dynamic in which they're more motivated in opposition to things they think might happen. For instance:More think gas prices will go up if Republicans win than if Democrats do.(Though they don't think Democrats will make gas prices go down.)Most voters don't think Democrats have a plan and won't make people financially better off, either...But more voters think they'll be worse off if Republicans win.The president remains a central factor. It would be a high number voting either to support or oppose a president in a midterm if this sentiment holds through Election Day. Most of the Democrats' voters are trying to oppose either President Trump or Republicans, even more than to help Democrats. (Whether that rationale ultimately limits Democrats' gains or not is another key question.)But he's motivating for most Republicans, especially MAGA.Some of this lead is attributed to more Democrats saying they'll either definitely vote, or have already voted early.But this is not over: The voters who describe themselves as only "probably" or "maybe" going to vote are more Republican. national.summary: The U.S. ambassador to the U.N. says the war with Iran could last another year, but he hopes Tehran will "come to the table" sooner.
national.body: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on Sunday called for a campaign to cut gas consumption by at least 10%, with officials anticipating shortages as winter approaches. While a major producer, Iran has long suffered shortages of natural gas, essential for powering heating systems, which have been exacerbated by war with the United States and Israel that began in February. During the most intense phase of the fighting, which lasted nearly 40 days, the two countries struck key Iranian infrastructure including natural gas refineries, according to Tehran. Winter in Iran often sees temperatures drop below freezing, especially in the country's north. "To get through the approaching winter, a nationwide effort is essential ... to reduce gas consumption by at least 10%," said Ghalibaf in a video carried by Iranian media. "Anyone who saves gas, regardless of the amount, will immediately receive the corresponding proceeds in their bank account, allowing everyone to see the tangible impact of those savings on their household budget." CBS/AFP

national.title: Kim Jong Un visits China to open new bridge, reaffirm ties
national.summary: The North Korean leader used the trip to reaffirm ties with its powerful neighbor.
national.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited China on Saturday, inaugurating a new bridge that connects the two countries and vowing to expand cooperation with his powerful neighbor.Kim's visit to China, the first in a year, is his latest move in an increasingly assertive foreign policy as he seeks to align Pyongyang with Beijing and Moscow in a united front against the United States under what he portrays as a "new Cold War."Kim arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong Saturday after crossing the newly opened bridge, according to South Korea's Unification Ministry and China's official Xinhua News Agency.In Dandong, Kim visited a memorial marking China's support of North Korea during the 1950-53 Korean War and met with Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of China's Communist Party.At the memorial, Kim said that the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) will "firmly carry forward the invincible DPRK-China friendship forged at the cost of blood all the time," according to the North's official Korean Central News Agency. During their meeting, Kim reaffirmed a resolve to develop bilateral cooperation, while Wang conveyed Chinese President Xi Jinping's greetings and said Kim's visit to the memorial was "of great significance" in carrying forward the friendship between the two countries, KCNA said.The two toured a car factory as well, before Wang accompanied Kim to the bridge to send him off, according to KCNA and Xinhua.While returning home via the bridge, Kim said "the bridge would undoubtedly and correctly fulfill its historic mission of linking the two countries and firmly joining the minds of the peoples of the two countries," KCNA reported.Kim has recently taken steps to bolster ties with China, the North's traditional main ally and economic lifeline, after years of prioritizing ties with Russia. China, for its part, has sought to restore its unique influence over North Korea.North Korea has sent thousands of troops and conventional weapons to support Russian President Vladimir Putin's war in Ukraine, possibly in exchange for military and economic assistance.Kim last visited Beijing in September 2025, when he met with Xi and watched a military parade alongside Putin and other foreign leaders.

national.title: Voters in Brazil head to polls as Lula goes up against Bolsonaro's son
national.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of Brazil's imprisoned ex-president, is challenging Lula, who is seeking a fourth term in office.
national.body:
Polls have opened in Brazil as people choose their new president in a closely fought run-off election.

The choice is between the 80-year-old incumbent, left-winger Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term in office, and right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro, 45.

Bolsonaro is the son of former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, who was sentenced to more than 20 years in jail for plotting a coup after losing the last election in 2022.

This is Bolsonaro's election to lose after he came top in the first round of voting on 4 October, which US President Donald Trump called a "very big" victory.

Never before has a candidate who trailed after the first round managed to overturn the deficit and win in the second round.

The younger Bolsonaro appeared at a polling station in Rio de Janeiro early on Sunday morning, telling reporters outside that "time has come for real change".

His supporters were jubilant at his final campaign rallies, confident that he would bring change to Brazil through his promised tough crackdown on organised crime, as well as tax and public spending cuts.

Bolsonaro campaigned on the eve of polls opening in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais, which has been a must-win state for any presidential hopeful since the 1980s.

national.title: The College of Magic turns ordinary kids into confident, top-hat wearing magicians
national.summary: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.
national.body:
Lubelo Mthenjana, who's 11, performs a magic trick involving fire during the annual junior magic contest at the College of Magic in Cape Town, South Africa. Tommy Trenchard for NPR hide caption

Dressed in a sharp black three-piece suit and a dapper yellow bow tie, Lubelo Mthenjana stands alone on a dark stage, taking in the last few seconds of quiet before the curtain opens. He takes a deep breath as his name is announced. Then he opens his arms wide and flashes a bright smile.

"Hello everyone! My name is Lubelo Mthenjana, and I will be performing for you … some magic!"

The audience of about 30 children and parents is spellbound. They laugh out loud as he makes a string of paper clips vanish into a plastic cup and gasp with surprise as the clips reappear inside a matchbox. Then comes his best trick: He conjures sweets out of thin air and tosses them into the crowd. The room erupts. As Lubelo takes his final bow to thunderous applause, his mom beams a proud smile at the 11-year-old apprentice magician.

On this cloudy Saturday morning in September, Cape Town's College of Magic is buzzing with energy as dozens of students are competing in the annual junior magic contest. Heading to their classrooms, children in top hats, crisp white shirts and ties dash up and down a staircase decorated with a riot of brightly colored posters. On every floor, display cabinets overflow with magic wands, sparkly hats, silk scarves, handcuffs, dice, Rubik's Cubes, toys, photographs and dozens of trophies earned by students in competitions all over the world.

Students examine a set of trick playing cards during a class at the College of Magic, whose pupils are ages 10 to 18. Tommy Trenchard for NPR hide caption

Aspiring magician Sibabalwe Sibaj, 17, juggles while riding a unicycle. Tommy Trenchard for NPR hide caption

Outside the old red-brick Victorian mansion, framed by palm trees, two teenage boys zip around the car park on unicycles. Balls, clubs and diabolos shoot up into the air as a handful of kids practice juggling on the porch.

national.title: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
national.summary: Nayib Bukele says bodies delivered to soldiers are "not our men" amid search for Salvadorans abducted last week.
national.body:
Four bodies handed over to special forces on a mission to Haiti to recover Salvadoran hostages are "not our men", El Salvador's president has said.

Nayib Bukele said a nongovernmental organisation delivered the human remains to one of Haiti's airports claiming they were four El Salvadoran air technicians, but that one of the corpses was a child's and another was wearing a different country's army uniform.

He had dispatched a military contingent, reportedly of hundreds of soldiers, on Thursday after the four men vanished after being ambushed by "heavily armed criminal groups".

The hostages had been part of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), which is tasked with tackling worsening gang violence in Haiti.

The men had been travelling back to their camp in an armoured vehicle when they were attacked in an area of the Caribbean island nation controlled by armed groups called Croix-des-Bouquets. No gang has so far claimed responsibility.

Bukele previously said the Salvadoran military operation in Haiti had the sole purpose of returning the four men alive. Approximately 450 soldiers had so far been deployed, according to Haitian newspaper Le Nouvelliste.

Bukele said the bodies the mission had received included one of a man of "considerably greater height than that of our air technicians", a person "who was wearing part of a uniform from an army that is not ours", and that among the remains were identification cards and uniforms from other countries.

He posted pictures showing the ID card of a GSF member and a corresponding national ID card from Chad in Africa.

national.title: More than 1,300 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
national.summary: Hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations in France, with protests also taking place in other European countries.
national.body:
More than 1,300 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France on Saturday that were followed by some clashes later in the day, officials have said.

After largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux.

Officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history.

The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000.

national.title: Musk says SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection as service restored
national.summary: The tech billionaire accuses Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using the network for military activity.
national.body:
Elon Musk has said his company SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink internet service, after Ukrainian officials said connectivity issues appeared to have been resolved.

The tech billionaire accused Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using it for military activity - but denied being responsible for a simultaneous issue with its US-run, military-grade counterpart Starshield.

Kyiv has not officially commented on Musk's latest claim but Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said his post was "very strange".

Musk had earlier denied deliberately throttling Ukraine's connection, which it says hampered its ability to conduct defensive operations for more than a week.

The issue first emerged last week during a broader row between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

Musk's latest comments, and the seeming restoration of the service, came after US President Donald Trump said he had told the Tesla and X owner to "put it back", having repeatedly denied instructing him to limit the service.

"Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be," Musk wrote on X on Saturday.

"Ukraine['s] military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week."

national.title: 'I cannot teach you integrity': How employee theft is hurting small businesses in Africa
national.summary: That Girl Boina's post about why she had closed her beauty parlour struck a nerve with other small business owners.
national.body:
When popular Kenyan food creator That Girl Boina took a two-week holiday to Europe, she expected to relax. A week into the trip, an Instagram direct message exposed a problem that would ultimately lead to the closure of her business.

"I was at your studio, I liked everything. The only problem was that I was asked to send money to a different number. It wasn't the number on the wall," a customer wrote to her.

Boina had opened Waxaholic Studio, a waxing and hydrafacial parlour in Nairobi's central business district, on 1 September 2024. A year later, she had hired a receptionist and two specialists and felt confident enough to take a two-week holiday, her first international trip of the year.

"I trusted them. It's two rooms and a reception - how do you mess that up?" she recalls thinking.

"It never occurred to me that maybe I was getting clients and someone else was stealing from me," she tells the BBC.

The discovery prompted Boina to examine the business more closely. Although the business had made a profit in the first few months, revenue began to fall in early 2025. She initially dismissed the decline as a seasonal slump but then realised there was a problem.

"Everyone around was making money apart from me," she says in hindsight.

She had already considered closing because it was not making a profit, but her initial investment, three employees depending on the business and her vision for it kept her going. The customer's message became the turning-point.

national.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe
national.summary: While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.
national.body:
Members of right-wing student groups march through the streets of Rome, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, during a demonstration called "Unlock Everything," organized in opposition to recent left-wing student protests and one of several demonstrations held by groups across the political spectrum. Gregorio Borgia/AP hide caption

MILAN — Thousands of young people marched Saturday through the streets of several Italian cities, including Milan, Rome and Turin, as authorities deployed large numbers of police and soldiers in a largely successful bid to stave off a repeat of the violent clashes and looting that marred similar protests last week.

The demonstration in Milan remained peaceful, but there were brief clashes with police in both Rome and Turin.

In Milan, thousands of young people marched the streets as soldiers were deployed and luxury boutiques were boarded up, but by late afternoon, most shops had opened, Italian media reported.

Premier Giorgia Meloni announced a raft of measures, including sending an additional 500 soldiers to Milan and tougher penalties for minors, who police said made up a large part of the violent protesters last week. In Milan, police detained several minors as a preventive measure, media reported.

While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.

The protests encompass a broad range of issues from education and corruption to anti-war movements, pensions and housing.

In Milan, huge crowds of mostly young people gathered as night fell, chanting insults to Meloni and holding aloft banners such as "No to lies of the state."

national.title: Why is Ukraine so reliant on Starlink and can Europe plug the gap?
national.summary: Ukraine needs another satellite internet service, but a decent alternative to Elon Musk's network doesn't exist - yet.
national.body:
Ukraine is in desperate need of a new satellite internet service, but a fast and reliable alternative to Elon Musk's Starlink network simply doesn't exist - yet.

Last week's sudden slowdown of the service in Ukraine, which affected Kyiv's ability to defend itself from Russian attacks, has shown how vulnerable the country can be, and sharply increased Europe's urgency to have its own military-grade satellite network.

That vulnerability was highlighted by Musk himself on Saturday, when he accused Ukraine of violating Starlink's terms of service by using it for "drone strikes to kill people".

Saying that loophole was closed last week, he wrote on X , external : "Violation of those terms will result in end of service."

He added: "Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately".

Published 15 October There are a few alternatives, but they are all lagging behind Starlink, which is the world's largest satellite constellation.

France's Eutelsat, with its OneWeb internet service, is the main alternative - but it only has about 600 active satellites, compared with Starlink's 10,000-plus.

The EU is working on a new network to rival Starlink, Iris², however it won't be up and running until 2029.

national.title: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates
national.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announces restrictions on the movement of Palestinian workers in the run-up to Tuesday's election.
national.body:
All West Bank land crossings will be closed during Tuesday's election in Israel, the country's military says, and Palestinian workers will be barred from entering all settlements.

The restrictions come amid a crackdown in the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the territory.

The Israel Defense Forces announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday.

It said most workers would also be barred from settlements from Sunday, with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other areas.

Before the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, more than 100,000 Palestinian workers were permitted to enter Israel. Since then only a small fraction have had their permits restored.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major operation on Friday in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed.

The Israeli military have been demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron, with hundreds of families having been displaced .

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced by the operation, which has led to at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened, according to footage shared online.

local.body:
Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper and the City of Dunkirk will host a Community Meeting on Tuesday at 5 p.m. via Zoom to share the Framework Plan for improvements to Wright Park Beach and Lake Front Boulevard, and to hear about the vision for the future of this important community waterfront.

The Wright Park Beach Shoreline Naturalization and Protection Project will focus on restoring and stabilizing the shoreline, bluffs, and habitat at Wright Park Beach. This popular Lake Erie destination has faced significant erosion from stormwater, lake level fluctuations, and waves as high as 30 feet -- damaging infrastructure and threatening the city's wastewater treatment plant.

In 2025, Dunkirk launched the design phase of this major shoreline protection effort in partnership with the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative (Cities Initiative), LimnoTech and SmithGroup, as part of the Cities Initiative's Resilient Coastal Projects Initiative with funding from the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation. Outreach and community discussion for the project is being facilitated by Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper.

For those interested, register to receive a link to the meeting: bnwaterkeeper.org/Dunkirk.

Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper is a community-based non-profit organization that protects and restores our waters and surrounding ecosystems for the benefit of current and future generations. For over 35 years, Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper has been the guardian of Western New York’s fresh water, protecting clean water, restoring the health of ecosystems, connecting people to the water and inspiring sustainable economic growth and community engagement. For more information on Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper, visit www.bnwaterkeeper.org.

The Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative is a multinational coalition of municipal and Indigenous government executives representing communities in the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence River Region who are working to promote economic prosperity in our communities and protect our fresh water for the benefit of current and future generations. With more than 425 member communities, the Cities Initiative is leading the way in advancing the environmental, economic, and social health of the region by addressing issues impacting its residents.

local.title: A Bedford patent offers a clue to frozen grape juice
local.summary: Frederick W. Bedford’s work with frozen juice concentrate went beyond freezing juice. A 1944 patent assigned to Bedford Products describes a way to recover more juice after concentrate was separated from ice. The patent uses grape juice as its example, but Bedford was not claiming the initial freezi
local.body:
Frederick W. Bedford's work with frozen juice concentrate went beyond freezing juice. A 1944 patent assigned to Bedford Products describes a way to recover more juice after concentrate was separated from ice.

The patent uses grape juice as its example, but Bedford was not claiming the initial freezing step. His process addressed juice solids that clung to the ice crystals: the remaining ice was crushed and washed in stages with portions of the same juice at different strengths, then processed through a centrifuge. Tanks, pumps and reservoirs moved the juice used in the washing stages so more juice could be recovered.

Figure 3 is a flow sheet for that recovery process. It identifies functional equipment such as a crusher, tank, centrifuge and pumps, but does not name manufacturers. The drawing documents the process Bedford patented; it cannot show which machines were installed at his Dunkirk plant or whether they came from Huntley Manufacturing, S. Howes or another maker.

Simplified process illustration is based on Figure 3 of U.S. Patent 2,354,633. It is not the original patent drawing and does not identify equipment suppliers or prove which machines were installed at Bedford's Dunkirk plant.

A local-history account also reports that Bedford sold its processing and storage plant to Red Wing soon after 1948 and that the Bedford company was sold in 1954. Red Wing made grape juice and fruit products, but the timing and scope of the reported transfer remain unresolved. Other materials point to a later National Dairy and Kraft connection. Available records do not establish what equipment or expertise may have moved between the businesses.

Former employees and families may help clarify the story through plant photographs, equipment nameplates, purchase or maintenance records, and recollections.

Patent details: U.S. Patent 2,354,633, "Process for Producing Fruit or Vegetable Juice Concentrate," filed May 22, 1943, and granted July 25, 1944. Frederick W. Bedford, inventor; assigned to Bedford Products.

local.title: For BOCES chef, culinary journey comes full circle
local.summary: For Chrissy Conklin, becoming a Culinary Arts instructor at the LoGuidice Educational Center is an opportunity to combine two things she has always enjoyed: cooking and education. Conklin brings nearly a decade of culinary industry experience to her new role with Erie 2-Chautauqua-Cattaraugus BOCES.
local.body:
For Chrissy Conklin, becoming a Culinary Arts instructor at the LoGuidice Educational Center is an opportunity to combine two things she has always enjoyed: cooking and education.

Conklin brings nearly a decade of culinary industry experience to her new role with Erie 2-Chautauqua-Cattaraugus BOCES. She also knows the Career & Technical Education experience from the student perspective, having completed the Culinary Arts program at the Hewes Educational Center while in high school.

That firsthand experience, along with her belief in the value of CTE and the importance of showing students there are options beyond a traditional college path, helped inspire her transition to teaching.

"There is so much value in CTE, and it's important for students to know there are options other than traditional college," Conklin said. "I've always had a passion for cooking and worked in the culinary industry for close to 10 years before switching to higher education. Teaching culinary arts at E2CCB allows me to combine two things I really enjoy."

One area Conklin is excited to explore with students is the wide range of food and culinary traditions found around the world. She plans to introduce students to different cultures, flavor profiles, cooking techniques and cuisines, giving them a broader understanding of the culinary field.

Students will also have opportunities to experience the fast-paced environment of a professional kitchen. Conklin plans to incorporate simulations that replicate the experience of working on a restaurant hotline, giving students a taste of what it takes to work efficiently and effectively as part of a kitchen team.

Along the way, she hopes students develop strong communication and teamwork skills alongside foundational culinary skills, including knife techniques and cooking methods.

"The culinary field is very rewarding, but it is hard work and takes an entire team to be successful," she said. "Once the students have knife skills and cooking techniques down, they should be able to take on any recipe!"

local.title: Special horses offer lifetime of trust, care
local.summary: Like people, horses have unique personalities. Are those personalities shaped by breeding, life experiences, or both? At Centaur Stride Therapeutic Riding Center, we have learned that while breeding may tell part of a horse’s story, their experiences and the trust they develops with people can make
local.body:
Like people, horses have unique personalities. Are those personalities shaped by breeding, life experiences, or both? At Centaur Stride Therapeutic Riding Center, we have learned that while breeding may tell part of a horse's story, their experiences and the trust they develops with people can make all the difference.

It is true that the horse lives in the present. That does not mean they do not have memory. It means they respond to immediate circumstances, whether it be threats, or loving trust.

For horses we take in on a trial basis, we can tell within 30 days if that horse has been abused or neglected to the point that recovery will take a long time, if at all. The horses go through extensive training and have to be approved for each specific rider or program. Since we must reduce the risk as much as possible, especially for people with disabilities, that 30 day trial is crucial.

But once a horse is fully accepted into our programs, they pretty much have a new lease on life, as long as they live.

Two of our most beloved horses, Kasie and Dyeak, are wonderful examples. Now 32 and 29, respectively, both have spent many years helping riders build confidence, develop skills and experience the special connection that horses can offer. Today, they enjoy retirement from riding lessons but continue to contribute through grooming and ground lessons.

Kasie, a Quarter Horse-Belgian cross mare, was donated to Centaur Stride on Aug. 24, 1994, when she was just five months old. Sandra Landrich of Fredonia donated Kasie along with her four-year-old full sister, Nikki. Apart from off-site training at age six by Pam Curtis, Kasie spent virtually her entire life here as a lesson and therapy horse. Retired from riding for about two years, she now enjoys long naps and time with her horse biddy, Pixie.

Dyeak, a Haflinger-Cob cross gelding, joined us on Feb. 17, 2001. He was purchased with funds donated by Ralph Wilson of Westfield. If we could clone a pony, Dyeak would be our first choice! Gentle and quiet from the beginning, he excelled with trail rides, therapeutic riding and advanced riders. Health issues eventually led to his retirement from riding lessons. Happily, he is doing much better and remains a favorite during grooming and ground lessons.

Our barn manager, Jean Lozier, works diligently to maintain the horses' physical health. Their well-being also depends on a suitable environment, meaningful activities and loving care. At Centaur Stride, we believe every horse deserves dignity and purpose throughout its life. Our riders and volunteers give them that purpose and much of the tender loving care they thrive upon.

The area of study for presentations this year is “Notable New Yorkers,” and in keeping with that theme, speaker Katherine Szewczuk, Vice President & Curator for the Dun
local.body:
The Fredonia Shakespeare Club opened its 2026-27 season with the traditional tea on Thursday, Oct. 8 at the Daisy Farm in Fredonia. The area of study for presentations this year is "Notable New Yorkers," and in keeping with that theme, speaker Katherine Szewczuk, Vice President & Curator for the Dunkirk Historical Museum, spoke on notable New Yorker Edna A. "Betty" Boorady.

Boorady was an American lawyer and diplomat born in Dunkirk. Miss Boorady graduated from St. Mary's Academy in Dunkirk in 1938, Fordham University in 1951, and the Cornell Law School in 1954. She was instrumental in the creation of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), founded in 1961 to counter the influence of the Soviet Union during the Cold War by means of soft power, using culture, political values, and foreign policies to enact change. Boorady was the first woman to direct an overseas mission of the USAID.

Boorady was awarded the Federal Woman's Award in 1974, a U.S. government honor highlighting the achievements of women in executive, professional, scientific, or technical roles across the federal career service and to encourage young women to join government service. She retired in 1986 and worked to establish the Boorady Reading Center in Dunkirk and was active in the League of Women Voters and the New York State Bar Association. Boorady died at the age of 87 in 2008.

The Fredonia Shakespeare Club is a historic literary and social club established in 1885 and has been unbroken since October,1886. Traditionally consisting of a dedicated group of members (historically around 20), the Club holds regular meetings, teas, lectures, and an annual picnic. Beyond studying Shakespeare and literature, the Club explores diverse historical, cultural, and global themes (such as UNESCO World Heritage sites, music histories, and local history) and attends regional theatrical productions. Current officers are Ms. Gail Crowe, President, Ms. Susan Westling, Vice President, Ms. Cheryll Rogers, Secretary, and Ms. Lisa Mertz, Treasurer. Meetings are generally held each Thursday afternoon.

local.title: Get big money out of politics
local.summary: It has been reported that the world’s richest man Elon Musk has poured more than $275 million into the Republican midterm election campaigns. Democrats are crying foul while Republicans will point out that George Soros and his family have donated more than $100 million in support of Democratic and p
local.body:
It has been reported that the world's richest man Elon Musk has poured more than $275 million into the Republican midterm election campaigns.

Democrats are crying foul while Republicans will point out that George Soros and his family have donated more than $100 million in support of Democratic and progressive causes in the 2026 midterm election cycle. $275 million from Musk! $100 million from Soros! Should any individuals have this much monetary influence in our state and national elections?

I encourage readers to use their cell phones and computers for more than just gossiping on Facebook and scrolling on TikTok. Take a look for yourselves at the astronomical money in politics today. A simple web search will yield a long list of the biggest donors to both parties in 2026. Donation figures can be found reaching back to the 2024 election cycle and beyond. While the total count of individual donors across the entire country has yet to be finalized by the Federal Election Committee, it is reported that roughly 80% of all election donation receipts in 2026 come from individuals contributing $100k or more. This in a country where the reported median income according to the U.S. Census Bureau is $87k. I wonder how many people reading this column could afford to donate $100k to a political party. I wonder how many people reading this column make $100k a year. For anyone, Republican, Democrat, Independent, Conservative or Liberal the money in politics today should be stomach turning.

I receive emails from the RNC and the DNC as well as from individual candidates, both Democrat and Republican, asking me for campaign donations as little as five dollars. They ask because my vote counts and even my meager donation to their party or to their cause can make a difference. It's kind of hard to feel like my vote in any statewide or national election will make a difference. A five dollar donation to a campaign would be .005% of the $100K that 80% of all donors put in. Not even a penny in comparison. I always vote on election day but I surely am not donating any money to any party or candidate. Both the Democrat and Republican parties are parties of the rich.

I have never cared for Donald Trump as a businessman, reality television personality, politician or president. I do understand the appeal Trump held for so many as he descended his golden escalator a decade ago. As a political outsider Trump promised to drain the swamp. He called out and insulted the deep pocketed Republican candidates who ran against him in the primaries. Trump stated that as a successful billionaire he could fund his own campaign and that he would not be beholden to business interests. Trump promised to repeal the Affordable Care Act and replace it with a better and more affordable health insurance program that would cover the entire country. He promised to lower prices and end forever wars. Trump vowed to settle the woke culture wars that the Democrats staunchly supported and that put off voters. While Trump has failed to live up to his promises, there is more money in politics than ever before. And Trump has enriched himself more than any other president in history. So much for draining the swamp.

local.body: David Pinero has captured six car accidents on the corner of Barton and West Ferry Streets through his home security camera. He has lived at that intersection for three years, but over the past two, he has seen an increase in crashes with one landing on his bushes.Pinero and his landlord both live at the corner house and told 7 news that they have filed a 311 with the City of Buffalo in hopes that new signs are put up at the intersection because they said that children live there and are worried about a tragedy that could be prevented."They're out of control and they're missiles," said Pinero. "You have kids going to school every day. They go up this street, they go up that street, they play in this yard in the summer. So, at any time, any of these cars that consistently either land up here or land over there are you're looking at a very terrible outcome, worst-case scenario, if that ever happens when they're out."The intersection is not a four-way stop, so Pinero said he believes the accidents are caused by the driver going down Barton Street, is making the assumption that West Ferry also has stop signs."So most of them stop. And then when they're satisfied that they see a car coming and it too will stop, they move forward, and that's a miscalculation. That's when you get your impacts," Pinero tells 7 News.7 News reached out to the city to see if they have taken Pinero's complaint. local.summary: Buffalo released its annual snow plan, but a mechanic shortage still threatens to keep the city's aging plow fleet off the roads this winter.
local.body: Buffalo has submitted its annual snow plan, but a shortage of mechanics threatens to keep snow plows off the streets when they break down. The city suffered the same problem last winter. Back in February, Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan revealed the city was down to just 14 working snow plows out of 36. Ryan blamed a combination of factors, including a lack of investment by previous administrations along with struggling to hire enough mechanics to fix the aging fleet."One of the reasons we're down so low is the city stopped properly paying its mechanics," the mayor said at the time.Eight months later, I visited the Broadway Barns to see how the city is preparing for the upcoming winter. I discovered recruiting mechanics is still a problem. There are just 12 mechanics to look after vehicles citywide says Kevin Savage, the city's superintendent of fleet maintenance. "Eight mechanics in this garage, two in police and two in fire," Savage said.Savage remembers when the shop was nearly twice as staffed, estimating there were around 22 mechanics back in 2009 when he first started working at the Broadway Barns. This year, the city has budgeted for close to that number — 20 mechanics. Pay remains a factor in the challenge to fill those positions, according to Deputy Mayor Benjamin Swanekamp. "Our pay's not competitive," Swanekamp said. "We included raises in the budget, but we're still negotiating with the union to try to get them to effectuate those."The average annual salary for an auto mechanic in the Buffalo area is around $53,000, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. local.title: Radiological investigation in Niagara, Erie counties narrows focus as cleanup planning moves forward
local.summary: State and federal teams have screened more than 1,000 properties, with around 40 referred to the EPA for further investigation. Some cleanup work could begin within weeks.
local.body: State and federal officials say they're narrowing the search for radioactive contamination in Western New York, with cleanup work potentially beginning at some properties in the coming weeks.Since July 23, teams have screened 1,094 properties in Niagara and Erie counties as part of the ongoing investigation. More than 907 property owners have been notified that no additional radiological investigation is needed, according to a new dashboard from the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation and the federal Environmental Protection Agency.Forty properties have been referred to the EPA for further investigation. Most are in the Town of Niagara and the City of Niagara Falls, with one in Grand Island. Four properties have received offers of voluntary temporary relocation, while owners of two other parcels declined additional assessment.The next step is more detailed sampling to determine where radioactive material is located, how much is present and what cleanup each property may require.EPA Region 2 Administrator Michael Martucci said some cleanup work could begin within the next couple of weeks. Officials hope to complete work that can be done before winter, while using the colder months to plan more extensive cleanup efforts for spring.Investigators are also conducting what the EPA calls forensic sampling — testing material to compare its characteristics with known historical sources. Officials have not established whether contamination at the various properties shares a common source.The federal government is separately seeking more than $12 million from a company over cleanup costs associated with radioactive waste found beneath two homes on Upper Mountain Road in Lewiston. Martucci said that case is specific to those properties and declined to speculate about any connection to other locations under investigation.Separately, the state is preparing additional environmental investigation at the former Witmer Road Drive-In site in the Town of Niagara, including areas along Gill Creek. Preparatory work will include fencing, signage and brush clearing.DEC Commissioner Amanda Lefton said that investigation is expected to continue into spring 2027.The next community drop-in session is scheduled for Nov. 10 from 4 to 7 p.m. at the Calvin K. There is a town proposition about whether to match other areas and provide a paid pension to volunteer firefighters.If approved, the proposition would add a Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP) that would give Barker Fire Department firefighters 10 years of monthly pension payments once they turn 65 years old.Firefighters would receive payments of $20 per month for every year of active service (ex., 12-year veteran = $240/month).Qualifying members would need at least five years of active service, and the payments max out at $400/month for 20 years or more of active service.The reason this requires a community vote is that it would be entirely paid for by a special property tax of $0.54 per $1,000 of assessed valuation.“It’s kind of a give-back program for our volunteers taking their time. We spend enough time away from our families,” Barker Fire Department President Stephen Horning said. “On average, they figured [the tax is] going to go up about $50 per household…. but the huge increase of running a full department if we were professionally paid would be astronomical and would not be feasible for the town of Somerset.”“You’re not going to get rich off of it, that’s for sure,” Town Supervisor Jeffrey Dewart said. "But it would be a little bit of an incentive to get new members and keep the ones we have.”WATCH: 'A give-back program': Somerset to vote on pensions for volunteer firefightersWhile not a universal program for departments across the county, fire companies in places such as Lockport, Lewiston and Newfane have already similar payments.This proposition also comes amid a busy year for the Barker Fire Department, as the seemingly ever-expanding Lake Mariner Data Center has increased use of the fire and EMT services.“Several times per week we’ve been there. local.body: October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and a Buffalo woman is sharing her journey with breast cancer to highlight the importance of early detection and knowing your body.For Lauren Lee and her husband, life has always revolved around staying active, traveling and exploring new places together. Originally from the Albany area, the couple moved to Buffalo eight years ago and dreamed of visiting every national park in the country.But in May, three months after her 30th birthday, Lee was diagnosed with stage 2 invasive ductal carcinoma, a type of breast cancer.“I found a lump and thought it was suspicious,” Lee said.The diagnosis forced the couple to put travel plans and social lives on hold as they shifted their focus on treatment.“We went from planning, like, park trips and going out with friends and things like that, to then changing all of that to being in an oncologist's that I felt so consumed with the diagnosis and depression that came along with it that it was really hard to see the light at the end of the tunnel.”She said completing chemotherapy has given her hope as she prepares for surgery.“The worst is behind me,” she said. “Chemotherapy was terrible, but surgery is next, and that's the next step in getting all of this out.”Lee hopes sharing her experience entertainment.title: Macklemore Speaks Out on Palestine and ICE at First Show Since Ed Sheeran Tour Exit
entertainment.summary: During a 17-song set at Colorado’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre, the rapper paused the show to address the crowd.
entertainment.body:
Macklemore returned to the stage Thursday night (Oct. 22) with a message that made clear he has no plans to retreat from the stance that preceded his removal from Ed Sheeran’s tour. Explore Macklemore See latest videos, charts and news

During a 17-song set at Colorado’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre, the rapper paused the show to address the crowd, calling for a “free Palestine ” while also speaking about Sudan, Congo, Lebanon, Haiti, and people affected by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Related Drake Turns 40, Shares Personal Childhood Photos: 'I Accept You for You' Jay-Z Brings Out Blue Ivy, John Legend, DJ Khaled & Scarface in Los Angeles Maluma Opens Up About Therapy and Finding Balance at Billboard Latin Music Week & More Uplifting Moments

“Being a human being in this moment is not complicated,” Macklemore said, according to footage from the concert. “It is not political. It is human to have a heart, to watch others suffering and to say, ‘Not anymore!’ So I say, free Palestine. I say, free Palestine!”

He continued: “I say, free Sudan. I say, free Congo, Lebanon, to Haiti, to all the people that are affected by ICE in America, who are afraid to leave their houses.”

The Red Rocks appearance marked Macklemore’s first concert since a turbulent run opening for Sheeran’s Loop Tour in September.

During two shows at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey , Macklemore called for Palestinian freedom from the stage and performed his 2024 protest song “Hind’s Hall” alongside imagery from Gaza. The performances prompted criticism from groups including the Israeli-American Council and ultimately led to his removal from the remaining dates.

Tour promoter Messina Touring Group said at the time that venues on the upcoming U.S. run had informed organizers they would not host the concerts with Macklemore on the lineup. Robert Kraft, whose Kraft Group owns Gillette Stadium , later confirmed that he had barred Macklemore from appearing at the Massachusetts venue, citing rhetoric and imagery that Kraft said had been offensive and hurtful to members of the Jewish community.

Sheeran subsequently stressed that the decision to remove Macklemore was not his, writing that it had been made by the promoter and venues. “I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes,” Sheeran said at the time, while adding that his own approach was to “maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed.”

entertainment.title: Jay-Z’s Victory Lap Continues as He Brings Out Blue Ivy Carter, John Legend, DJ Khaled for SoFi Stadium Opening Night
entertainment.summary: The rapper also brought out Scarface as a special guest for the first of two much anticipated L.A. shows on Friday night.
entertainment.body:
“I’ve been away too long,” Jay-Z told a hyped-up SoFi Stadium crowd soon after taking the stage on Friday night. The rap icon was met with cheers as he, at last, brought his yearlong victory tour to Los Angeles.

Indeed, it’s been close to a decade since Jay last played a full-fledged solo concert in the city, with Shawn Carter closing out his 4:44 Tour across the street at the Forum in 2017 and playing the Rose Bowl for his joint On the Run Tour with Beyoncé a year later. After a historic three-night run in New York at Yankee Stadium and a few more shows in London and Paris, not to mention an eight-part HBO docuseries directed by Rick Rubin, it’s finally L.A.’s turn, as Jay kicked off the first of two much-anticipated concerts Friday night in celebration of the 30th anniversary of his debut album Reasonable Doubt and 25th anniversary of The Blueprint. Related Stories Music Young Miko Gets Flirty With L.A. During Her Late Checkout Tour Music Feds Sue Ticket Broker Firm Over Alleged $120M Scheme For Beyoncé, Pitbull Tickets

The result was a career-spanning tour de force from one of hip-hop’s most seminal figures, and perhaps more Yankee hats and jerseys in the crowd than SoFi Stadium has ever seen. Kicking off just before 9:30 p.m. local time, the show opened with a video of Jay and Beyoncé alone in the seats at Yankee Stadium, with Bey behind him playing with her husband’s hair.

Flanked by an impressive backing band and starting the night with “Hovi Baby,” Jay powered through a collection of hits and fan favorites for two hours, from “FuckWithMeYouKnowIGotIt” to “Run This Town,” “Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem),” “Lucifer” and “99 Problems.”

“Let me take you back to my home for a second,” Jay told the crowd before launching into “Empire State of Mind” toward the end of the evening.

Whereas Jay brought an overwhelming set of surprise superstar guests to his shows in New York, including Eminem, Rihanna, Nas, Usher and wife Beyoncé, L.A.’s opening night was comparably subdued in that department as he performed much more by himself. Still, his daughter Blue Ivy did come out on the keys for “The Story of O.J.” and “Dead Presidents,” while Scarface joined for “This Can’t Be Life” and “Mind Playing Tricks on Me.” DJ Khaled and John Legend helped close it down for the last song for “God Did.”

Much of the audience was of course waiting in anticipation Friday night wondering if Jay would address or confirm the reports that he’d chosen himself as headliner for the Super Bowl Halftime show in February. It’d have been a perfect time to make any news on the matter, performing in the very venue hosting the big game, though the world will have to wait, as Jay didn’t so much as reference the news on Friday, keeping it very much about the current show at hand.

entertainment.summary: Hedge fund jerks and private equity bros are being pilloried by popular creator comedians — and the finance world is laughing along.
entertainment.body:
Johnny Hilbrant Partridge never worked an hour on Wall Street, but you’d never guess that by looking at him. Nearly every day, Partridge takes to YouTube to channel his inner finance bro as P.E. Guy, a puffer-vested private equity putz who brags about his million-dollar deals, Aspen manse and private plane.

Partridge, who once taught fitness classes in Boston, debuted the character on social media last year, which boosted his following beyond Barry’s and SoulCycle devotees. Today, he has 400,000-plus Instagram followers, up from 7,000 about 18 months ago. Related Stories Influence Peddlers Top Creators' Secret Weapon? Indian Video Editors Movies Lowden, Turner or a Dark Horse: One James Bond Casting Test Has Nothing to Do With Acting

Although Partridge lampoons private equity, his skits resonate beyond buyout boys. “I think a lot of people have that experience of coming in contact with somebody who wants to one-up you and make you feel like they win the conversation because they have an impressive-sounding job,” he says.

As certain business figures become as talked about as celebrities, Wall Street yuksters like Partridge are surging on social media. While memes still flood finance bro DMs, creator-helmed videos are gaining momentum on both Wall Street and Main Street. Some riff on Bloomberg headlines, while others simply play on C-suite stereotypes.

Other creators skewering corporate life include The Swiss Chris (442,000 Instagram followers), who portrays a highfalutin European banker; Clemente Varas Collado (115,000 Instagram followers), who frequently roasts asset manager BlackRock, and engineer-turned-entertainer Varun Rana (90,000 Instagram followers).

It’s not an entirely new trend — Wall Street meme pages have been around for over a decade — but social media algorithms are increasingly favoring shortform video, benefiting creator-actors over anonymous meme lords. It’s led to stalling growth for some picture-heavy accounts, including Trust Fund Terry, which launched about eight years ago on Instagram.

Trust Fund Terry has never revealed his identity, though he admits on the phone that he has toiled in consulting and finance. Terry, a pseudonym, said audience building on Instagram has become more difficult thanks to Reels. “I think they’ve really been trying to push the more traditional creators, where they’re telling a story in either short or longform video,” he said.

entertainment.title: Lowden, Turner or a Dark Horse: One James Bond Casting Test Has Nothing to Do With Acting
entertainment.summary: There are some not-so-secret behind-the-scenes qualities that Bond producers are looking for.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Final James Bond screen tests have begun, which means there’s a chance that while you’re reading this an actor is auditioning in London for the biggest role of their life, a casting that could make its mark on one of the world’s longest-running film franchises.

The oddsmakers — taking a cue from The Hollywood Reporter and others’ reporting — suggest Jack Lowden and Callum Turner are the favorites . Both have their apparent pros and cons.

Lowden has a very likable presence on Apple TV’s Slow Horses , where he plays MI5 agent River Cartwright. For years, the role has looked like an audition for Bond. All the things Bond does — drama, action, romance, stunts — are on display, even though Lowden’s character has a rather different low-key vibe than 007. He’s an everyman pick, and that’s a rather refreshing idea that would give Bond writers new notes to explore with the character. Related Stories General News Hannah Einbinder Says Speaking Out for Palestine Is "the Bare Minimum" Movies Jack Lowden, Margaret Qualley Top Bookie Odds for Next James Bond and Bond Girl

Turner looks like he might have been grown in a lab to play Bond, which is the best thing about him as a choice, but also a potential detriment if producers want somebody who feels more original. He seems could be perfect for the part — handsome and suave and posh. Between him and Lowden, Turner would also likely win the sex appeal contest.

Reportedly in the mix are Jack O’Connell and Josh O’Connor — two actors with such similar names one wonders if sources leaking to the press got the two mixed up and only one of them is actually auditioning.

Regardless of who gets the part, there is a lot more to playing Bond than merely fighting and bantering and firing a Walther PPK.

There are qualities that many pundits on the sidelines might overlook, but Bond’s producers most assuredly will not: Bond may be a rogue character who plays by his own rules, but the actor cast in the role has to be the ultimate team player. Bond is a massive commitment that requires an actor to adhere to the highest professional standards for more than a decade. The actor may not always be playing Bond, but will forever be a Bond, and therefore must be counted upon to not embarrass the franchise.

This means the choice should be somebody who, for instance, isn’t going to sound off divisively about politics, get into messy domestic disputes or start going on public benders. More subtly, it means somebody who’s down to be an agreeable brand ambassador for the part, who will treat fans respectfully and gamely participate in the intense media circus which accompanies every Bond film.

entertainment.title: Anthropic Sued For Stealing Elvis Presley Music to Train AI: ‘Deeply Protective of These Iconic Songs’
entertainment.summary: The owners of The King's IP are cracking down on the tech giant, adding one of music's most legendary figures to the massive legal battle over AI music.
entertainment.body:
The owners of Elvis Presley ‘s music have launched a legal war over artificial intelligence, suing AI giant Anthropic over accusations that it trained its models on hundreds of the legendary artist’s song without permission.

Though music companies like Universal Music Group have already repeatedly sued AI companies for stealing their IP, the new lawsuits represents by far the most high-profile legal action filed on behalf of an individual musician — in this case, arguably the most famous recording artist of all time.

The case was filed by a unit of Authentic Brands Group, the licensing giant that largely controls the intellectual property rights to Elvis, including much of his song catalog, his brand trademarks and the rights to his name, image and likeness. It was co-filed by various other entities that own Elvis rights.

Litigation over AI music has centered more on Suno, the leading AI song generator, which was sued in 2024 by all three major music companies over such training accusations. It eventually settled with Warner Music Group last year and has vowed to partner with the music industry, but is still facing contentious litigation from UMG and Sony Music. Anthropic, a far larger AI firm, has faced similar cases across creative industries, including from music publishers .

The new case Friday largely mirrors those earlier cases, claiming Anthropic illegally used music en masse to create technology that produces “unlicensed derivative works.” But it centers on what the Elvis plaintiffs call “some of the most groundbreaking, revolutionary, influential, and enduring musical compositions in human history.”

That includes “Can’t Help,” arguably Presley’s most famous song, “Don’t Be Cruel,” one of his early massive hits, and “Little Less,” which saw a resurgence in popularity due to a 2000s remix. The lawsuit also cites “All Shook Up,” “Return to Sender” and “(You’re The) Devil in Disguise”.

A rep for Anthropic did not immediately return a request for comment on Saturday.

Maluma spoke candidly about therapy, anxiety, fatherhood and the challenge of balancing family life with a demanding career during the “Like Minded” conversation at Billboard Latin Music Week on Wednesday (Oct. 21). Moderated by Billboard ’s co-chief content officer Leila Cobo, the BetterHelp-presented session also featured bilingual therapist Patricia Arrieta. Related Macklemore Speaks Out on Palestine and ICE at First Show Since Ed Sheeran Tour Exit Drake Turns 40, Shares Personal Childhood Photos: 'I Accept You for You' Jay-Z Brings Out Blue Ivy, John Legend, DJ Khaled & Scarface in Los Angeles

The conversation came shortly after the birth of Maluma’s second child, Orion, whom he said has brought him a new sense of calm and clarity. “I’ve finally been able to find that balance between my personal life and my artistic career,” he said. The Colombian star described therapy as an ongoing practice rather than a quick fix. “For me, therapy is being quiet, it is meditation, it’s constantly feeling uncomfortable and learning to love that discomfort,” he said.

Maluma acknowledged that he still experiences anxiety while managing his responsibilities as a father, artist, entrepreneur and leader of a large team. After undergoing a tension headache during an especially demanding week, he used ChatGPT to help organize his schedule and prioritize his well-being. “I started prioritizing my peace, lowering my burdens and stress,” he said. “I need at least four hours in the afternoon to spend with my family.”

He also spoke about moving away from extreme approaches to fitness and developing a healthier relationship with food and his body. “If you love yourself, you make good decisions,” he said. “My health is not negotiable.”

Reflecting on his latest album, Loco por Volver , Maluma said the project became part of his personal transformation. “It was the album that gave me back so many things I had lost,” he said. “The music transformed me.”

What began as a live songwriting experiment at last year’s Billboard Latin Music Week became a finished release — and then a Billboard Latin Music Awards performance on Thursday (Oct. 22). entertainment.title: Drake Sings ‘I Want It That Way’ With Backstreet Boys at 40th Birthday Bash
entertainment.summary: The rapper capped a week of festivities with a lavish New York celebration — complete with designer gifts and a $1 million game show.
entertainment.body:
Drake rang in his 40th birthday with more than 400 guests, million-dollar prizes and a surprise performance from the Backstreet Boys — one day after adding another record to his already historic résumé. Explore Drake See latest videos, charts and news

The Toronto superstar celebrated at New York ’s Casa Cipriani on Friday night (Oct. 23), hours before officially turning 40 on Oct. 24. According to TMZ, guests were treated to luxury giveaways including Chanel and Hermès handbags, while a game show held during the party offered cash prizes ranging from tens of thousands of dollars up to $1 million. Related Jay-Z Brings Out Blue Ivy, John Legend, DJ Khaled & Scarface in Los Angeles Maluma Opens Up About Therapy and Finding Balance at Billboard Latin Music Week & More Uplifting Moments Drake Becomes First Act to Surpass 350 Million RIAA-Certified Units, With 30 New Certifications

The night’s biggest musical surprise came courtesy of the Backstreet Boys, who performed for the crowd before Drake joined them onstage for their 1999 hit “ I Want It That Way .”

Amid the spectacle, Drake took a moment to reflect on the milestone.

“Tonight isn’t about a tour, an album release, or a bunch of videos we shot,” he told the room. “It’s about being alive, staying alive.”

The New York celebration capped several days of birthday festivities that began back home in Toronto. Earlier in the week, Drake gathered with friends at the CN Tower, where he was surprised with a collage of photos and memories. Popcaan was among those in attendance.

Drake later traveled to New York with his mother and members of his entourage aboard Air Drake, his customized Boeing 767, and was spotted dining at SoHo restaurant Mamo on Thursday night (Oct. 22).

The Backstreet Boys appearance also carried some history. In July 2022, the group brought Drake onstage during their DNA World Tour stop at Toronto’s Budweiser Stage and introduced him as their “sixth member” before performing “I Want It That Way.”
